pages.title: celld system architecture
pages.purpose: Explain the overall system: node/fleet/cell concepts, the crate layering (celld-logic decision core, celld adapter shell, celld-ltx replication library), the single-actor execution model, and the primary control/data flows.
instructions: Cite concrete source evidence for every non-obvious technical claim, preferring bounded repo:// spans.

pages.title: Cell lifecycle, routing, alarms, cron, and WebSockets
pages.purpose: Explain Durable Object cell states (inactive, dormant/hibernated, resident, remote, fenced), the phase machine and activation path, request routing, alarms and wake entries, cron triggers, and WebSocket kinds.
instructions: Ground each phase and transition in the Phase enum and on_event logic; cite the phase machine source.

pages.title: Change guides for common maintenance tasks
pages.purpose: Focused, step-by-step change guides for representative tasks: adding a new environment variable, adding a new Workers API binding, modifying the coordination protocol, and updating the compatibility surface.
instructions: Write concrete, code-grounded steps that point at the exact files and seams to change; mark uncertainty.

pages.title: Deployments, Wrangler configuration, and in-place adoption
pages.purpose: Explain celld deploy, the supported Wrangler config subset, the deployment objects and manifest contract, feature gates, static assets, and how nodes adopt a new deployment in place via generations.
instructions: Ground config keys and deployment objects in deploy.rs and protocol.rs; list refused keys from SUPPORTED_KEYS and the compat doc.

pages.title: Memory management and pressure shedding
pages.purpose: Explain memory sampling (RSS, jemalloc slack, cgroup working set), the pressure watermarks and latches, the shedding walk down, V8 heap limits, and resident-cell admission caps.
instructions: Ground watermarks and release rules in pressure.rs; explain the two independent latches precisely.

pages.title: Node lifecycle: lease, fencing, graceful shutdown, and rolling updates
pages.purpose: Explain the node lease protocol, self-fencing, the first-readiness gate, graceful shutdown with batched cell handoff, the drain token, dead-node GC, and rolling-update version constraints.
instructions: Ground lease timing and fencing in the logic core and guarantees.md; document the per-version upgrade constraints from the docs.

pages.title: Object storage: bucket providers, credentials, and conditional writes
pages.purpose: Explain the single object-store client, the three conditional-write dialects (S3 etag, GCS generation, Azure etag), provider credentials, reserved bucket prefixes, the storage test, and bucket key prefixes.
instructions: Ground the dialect and error contracts in bucket.rs; note qualified vs unqualified stores from docs.

pages.title: CLI and internal operator API
pages.purpose: Explain the celld command-line surface (run, diagnose, cell, d1, kv, queue, deploy, dev), the stdout-is-data rule, and the internal listener operator API (/state, /reload, /shutdown, /cell, /do, /runtime).
instructions: Document command groups from cli.rs and the operator routes from the code; note the alpha status of the operator API.

pages.title: Cell ownership, fencing, and the RPO=0 durability protocol
pages.purpose: Explain how exactly-one-owner is enforced with conditional bucket writes and fencing epochs, how writes are acknowledged only after a durability proof (output gate), the fleet vs bucket proof paths, self-fencing, and the storage qualification test.
instructions: Treat docs/guarantees.md as narrative; verify each claim against the ownership_store, logic core, and bucket adapters.

pages.title: SQLite replication, LTX format, and the fleet log tier
pages.purpose: Explain how each cell's SQLite WAL is captured as LTX data, the LTX v0.5.2 file format, object layout under cells/<cell>/ltx/e<epoch>/, level tiering and compaction, and the in-fleet replicated node-log that enables fleet-durable writes.
instructions: Describe the format and protocol from the source; do not invent guarantees beyond what the code and guarantees.md establish.

pages.title: V8 isolates and the Workers runtime surface
pages.purpose: Explain the V8 isolate-per-cell execution model, the Workers/Durable Objects runtime API surface, storage ops, WebSocket handling, wasm support, Worker Loader, and the Cloudflare compatibility boundary.
instructions: Document the compatibility surface from cloudflare-compat.md and the js adapter source; mark unsupported APIs as gaps.

pages.title: Security boundary and fleet authentication
pages.purpose: Explain the trust boundary, public vs internal listeners, the fleet HMAC peer authentication with clock limit and replay protection, the peer tunnel, forwarded-header policy, and bucket credential authority.
instructions: Ground the HMAC headers, clock window, and replay cache in peer_auth.rs; keep the alpha boundary honest from security.md.

pages.title: Telemetry: traces and logs
pages.purpose: Explain the opt-in telemetry system: span/log recording, the Parquet bucket sink and OTLP sink, schema, sampling, flushing, retention, and the DuckDB query workflow.
instructions: Ground sinks, schema version, and flush behavior in telemetry.rs and docs/telemetry.md.

pages.title: Testing strategy: conformance, model checking, simulation, and live fleets
pages.purpose: Explain how celld tests its three promises: differential conformance against workerd, TLA+ model checking, deterministic simulation of the decision core, and fault-injected live fleet labs.
instructions: Ground the simulation architecture in the logic core and the conformance test includes in celld/lib.rs.

pages.title: celld quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical entry point: install, run celld dev locally, deploy a Wrangler project to a bucket, start fleet nodes, and try the bundled examples.
instructions: Ground commands and defaults in source and docs; mark anything the repository does not establish as uncertain.
